added.summary: A film choice tagged `#hotspot:<id>` is also taken by clicking that hotspot on the picture: a segment's `track hotspot` gives each `id` a `rect x y width height` (fractions of the video frame) that moves between its keys, or `off true` to end it. FilmView.hotspots gives the hotspots of the window's enabled choices. A choice tagged `#qte:press:<action>`, `#qte:hold:<action>:<ms>` or `#qte:mash:<action>:<presses>` is taken by that og.input action in the window (one press, held that long, or that many presses; a hold let go starts again); og.film counts it and FilmView.qtes gives each one's progress. Only a node's first 8 choices may be a QTE. The cook refuses a `#hotspot` id its segment has no key for, a `#qte` that is none of the forms, and a QTE past the eighth choice.

`track hotspot { key <t> { id "<id>" rect <x> <y> <w> <h> } }`: from its key the hotspot `id` covers `rect` (fractions of the video frame from its top left), moving linearly to the same id's next key and held after its last until a key `off true`. Nothing draws it; og.film offers a `#hotspot:<id>` choice there. The kind joins TimelineTrackInfo.kind.

Skips the playing segment to its window's open (film.open) when that is ahead, else to its cut, which takes the pending or default choice: for replaying a seen segment. Command film:skip. Refused once the film has ended.

A film node headed `og-film-dissolve: <seconds>` (0 to 5) dissolves its segment in over the one before, which plays on under it for that long: og.Film.previous, dissolve and dissolveLeft, FilmView.previous (the old picture) and mix (the new one's opacity over it). Without the header the cut is hard.

A prepared dialogue's film nodes laid out as a flowchart: FilmChart.nodes (each with its depth, the fewest film nodes from the start, and an x and y in NodeGraph units) and links (where each node may lead, through logic nodes, with the choice index and an SVG curve). The built-in film-flowchart screen draws it.

added.summary: film-flowchart draws og.film.chart with the built-in NodeGraph (the story so far, seen nodes marked). film-chapters lists og.film.load's chapters as cards to play from, locked until reached. film-gallery lists its endings the same way. film-choices now draws a choice's hotspot over the picture and a quick-time event's progress under its choice.
